metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., >40% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 3–7% for next 3–7 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model often fails to adjust quickly; add 2–5% upward bias for next 2–4 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the window (first 5–7 days); apply a 3–5% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent highs; use 3-day moving average of past 30d to anchor forecast.
